frames.narration: An employee of Globex opens globex.example.com/invoices with an access token. The router reads the tenant from the host name and from the signed claim in the token. Both say 'globex', so the tenant is trusted. A request whose host and token disagree would be rejected here.

The router looks the tenant up in its cached copy of the directory: pooled tier, shard 1, region eu, schema version 42, status active. The lookup takes microseconds, and the cache refreshes every few seconds, so a moved tenant is found quickly.

The router checks Globex's token bucket: 18 requests in the last second, against a plan limit of 50. It passes. A neighbour with a burst would have been given a 429 at this point, with a Retry-After, without ever reaching the database.
The app opens a transaction on shard 1 and sets the tenant for the session (SET LOCAL app.tenant = globex). The list-invoices query is written by a developer who forgot the 'where tenant_id' clause.

The row-level security policy adds the condition itself, so the shard returns Globex's 6 invoices and not the 280 rows of the 80 tenants stored beside them. The bug is real, but it cannot leak. A test in the build would have caught the missing filter before release.

The app looks for a cached copy of the page settings. The key is built by one helper, t:globex:settings:v3, so another tenant with the same setting name could never be served this entry. The answer goes back to the employee.
The call is a billable event. The app puts a small record on the usage queue: tenant globex, metric api_call, quantity 1, event id e-7f3a. It returns nothing the user waits for.

An aggregator reads the queue and adds the event to Globex's total for this hour. If the same event id arrives a second time, it is ignored, so a retry cannot double count. At the end of the month the billing job turns the hourly totals and the plan into invoice lines.
